_meta.indication: Carbaglu (carglumic acid) is indicated as adjunctive therapy for the treatment of acute hyperammonemia, and as maintenance therapy for the treatment of chronic hyperammonemia, due to the deficiency of the hepatic enzyme N-acetylglutamate synthase (NAGS).

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Retrospective review of the clinical course of 23 NAGS deficiency patients treated with carglumic acid (Orphan Europe retrospective case series)
pivotal_trials.phase: Open-label, uncontrolled retrospective case series (no prospective controlled trials)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, uncontrolled retrospective review of clinical courses of patients treated with carglumic acid 100 to 250 mg/kg/day orally
pivotal_trials.population: Patients from birth to adulthood with hyperammonemia due to N-acetylglutamate synthase (NAGS) deficiency; all began treatment during infancy or childhood
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Short-term plasma ammonia level (within 7 days after first carglumic acid treatment); long-term maintenance of normal ammonia assessed as persistence of efficacy
pivotal_trials.n: N=23 total patients; 21 included in the efficacy analysis (2 excluded for heterozygote NAGS mutation and asymptomatic status)
pivotal_trials.result: Baseline mean ammonia 218.9 µmol/L (median 142.0); reduction observed within 24 hours of first dose and normal plasma ammonia levels attained by day 3; long-term (last available value) mean 51.8 µmol/L (median 25.0). Normal range 5 to 50 µmol/L.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (occurring in ≥13% of patients) regardless of causality were vomiting (26%), abdominal pain (17%), pyrexia (17%), anemia (13%), ear infection (13%), and diarrhea (13%), as well as tonsillitis, nasopharyngitis, and headache.
target_moa: Carglumic acid is a synthetic structural analogue of N-acetylglutamate (NAG), the essential allosteric activator of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 (CPS 1), the first enzyme of the urea cycle; it replaces NAG (the product of NAGS) to activate CPS 1 and allow ammonia to be converted into urea.
modality: Small molecule (synthetic structural analogue of N-acetylglutamate)

advisory_committee.vote: Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee convened January 13, 2010; it voted unanimously (Yes: 12, No: 0, Abstain: 0) that the risk/benefit profile supports approval for treatment of hyperammonemia in NAGS deficiency.

summary.text: Carbaglu was approved via a Priority NDA for NAGS deficiency, a rare urea cycle disorder, with orphan drug designation (granted January 20, 1998). Efficacy was based on an open-label, uncontrolled retrospective case series of 23 NAGS deficiency patients, and an Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee convened January 13, 2010 voted unanimously (12-0) that the risk/benefit supports approval. Approval carried postmarketing requirements including a 2-year carcinogenicity study and a long-term patient registry.

requirement.text: 1604-2. A registry of patients, including infants, with NAGS deficiency being treated with carglumic acid to obtain long-term clinical safety information.

citations.quote: 1604-2. A registry of patients, including infants, with NAGS deficiency being treated with carglumic acid to obtain long-term clinical safety information. Data to be collected will include patient demographics, details of treatment with carglumic acid, other therapies for hyperammonemia, dietary protein management, clinical status, neurocognitive and psychomotor status, growth and development status, and adverse events.

requirement.text: 1604-3. A study of the effects of carglumic acid on pregnancy and fetal outcomes (may be a sub-study within the NAGS deficiency registry).

citations.quote: 1604-3. A study of the effects of carglumic acid on pregnancy and fetal outcomes. This study can be performed as a sub-study within the registry for all patients with NAGS deficiency. Information on pregnancy and fetal outcomes should be submitted annually (in annual reports) and included in the final report submission on the registry at 15 years post-approval.

requirement.text: 1604-4. Complete and submit the final study report for the ongoing in vitro metabolic stability study of N-carbamyl [14C]-glutamic acid in rat, mini-pig, dog, monkey and human hepatocytes.

citations.quote: 1604-4. We acknowledge your plans to complete and submit the final study report for the ongoing study entitled, "In *vitro* metabolic stability of N-carbamyl [14C]-glutamic acid in rat, mini-pig, dog, monkey and human hepatocytes." The viability of the hepatocytes in terms of various cytochrome P450 enzyme activities should be documented in the report.
